hints: Differentiate $y=\theta+2\cos\theta$ to get $1-2\sin\theta$, and apply the quotient rule carefully to $x=\dfrac{\cos\theta}{2-\sin\theta}$.
In the numerator of $dx/d\theta$, use $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$ to expose a factor related to $1-2\sin\theta$.
Divide the two parameter derivatives and cancel the common factor to reach the required squared expression.
walkthrough:
Differentiate $x = \dfrac{\cos\theta}{2 - \sin\theta}$ with respect to $\theta$ using the quotient rule $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\theta}\left(\dfrac{u}{v}\right) = \dfrac{u'v - uv'}{v^2}$:
$$u = \cos\theta \implies u' = -\sin\theta$$
$$v = 2 - \sin\theta \implies v' = -\cos\theta$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}\theta} = \dfrac{(-\sin\theta)(2 - \sin\theta) - (\cos\theta)(-\cos\theta)}{(2 - \sin\theta)^2}$$

Simplify the numerator of $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}\theta}$ using the Pythagorean identity $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$:
$$\text{Numerator} = -2\sin\theta + \sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1 - 2\sin\theta$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}\theta} = \dfrac{1 - 2\sin\theta}{(2 - \sin\theta)^2}$$

ai_rubric.Differentiating Parametric Curves: Identifies $\frac{dy}{d\theta}=1-2\sin\theta$; Derives $\frac{dx}{d\theta}=\frac{-2\sin\theta+\sin^2\theta-\cos^2\theta}{(2-\sin\theta)^2}$ or equivalent; Concludes with $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=(2-\sin\theta)^2$.
